top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye. The idea is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes: the light shift cancels on the clock transition, so many neutral atoms combine ion-level accuracy with ensemble statistics. The physics is mature, reproduced near 10^-18 by independent laboratories, and the two-name allocation is a defensible judgement. The citation names trapped neutral atoms and the magic wavelength, which carries the distinction from earlier metrology prizes. No award is clearly inferior.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my documented collaborators (L'Huillier and the Lund group, Keller at ETH, Schuch, Dahlstrom, Argenti, Indelicato) are not among Katori or Ye, only general proximity to precision atomic physics
